# Vendored Vino userspace core

Source: https://github.com/cameron1729/Vino, commit `490aa8e13488c9dbf0c88cb80aa4676d525a50ef` (2026-09-21), directory `revdi/`.

| Directory | Upstream | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| `chimera/` | `revdi/chimera` | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `kernel-shim/` | `revdi/kernel-shim` | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `vino-driver/` | `revdi/vino-driver` | GPL-2.0-or-later |
| `LICENSES/` | `revdi/LICENSES` | licence texts |

Copied unmodified except for the local patches below. `chimera/vino/` holds the literal DL3 protocol, HDCP 2.2 AKE, encrypted control plane, dock profiles, and video codec from the in-kernel `drm/vino` driver; chimera compiles it in userspace over libusb.

## Local patches

Patches 1–7 were found or measured on a Humanscale M/Connect 2 (`17e9:600f`, Ridge firmware 12.2.25) with two HP Z27k G3 monitors. Later patches below are source-review improvements; their measurement and hardware-validation status is stated separately.

1. **Parallel encode** — `chimera/src/scanout.rs`: `strip_hashes` and the fresh-body pass of `HeadScanout::encode` run across cores through `par_for_each_mut` (scoped threads; passes under 64 strips stay on the calling thread). Upstream's only SIMD path is x86-64, so on Apple Silicon a serial 4K keyframe took 96 ms; parallel it takes 12 ms. Output is byte-identical to serial `encode_strip` + `frame_records` across all 8100 strips of a 4K frame.
2. **EDID readiness gate** — `chimera/src/edid_fetch.rs`: before the dock reports its downstream read complete, only the dock's own `NVT` placeholder EDID is discarded (`is_dock_placeholder`). This dock never sets the readiness bit, so upstream discarded both monitors' real `HPN` EDIDs and lit nothing.
3. **Downstream-change notice** — `chimera/src/session.rs`: replies read by `send_control` and `send_control_echoing` go through `ControlSession::receive`, which records the dock's `id=0x03 sub=0x82` push; `take_downstream_change()` exposes it. The engine probes lit heads only after this notice on shared-EDID-handler docks, because probing them once a second kept both monitors in standby.
4. **Settle pass** — `chimera/src/scanout.rs` (`HeadScanout::settle`, `touched`) and `chimera/src/session.rs` (`ControlSession::settle`): every strip changed since the last settle is owed another `damage_frames` round once the surface has been still for 100 ms. The engine paces those retransmissions one refresh apart. A transmission the dock missed or placed in the other buffer while things moved can therefore not leave a stale box behind.
5. **Video bytes returned** — `ControlSession::present_rgb` returns the bytes it submitted so the engine can hold all heads together to 100 MB/s (Vino's measured DLM rate on this family). Unthrottled full-screen motion on two 4K heads reset the dock off the bus within minutes.
6. **Three ring slots** — `chimera/vino/profile.rs`: Ridge `dock_buffers: 3` and `FrameDelivery::new(3, 1, 3)` (upstream 2 and `(2, 1, 3)`); the pinned assertion in `api.rs` follows. Ridge's frame trailer already cycles three phases (`ring_phase`, `seq % 3`), and Vino's notes record the vendor filling slots 0/2/4 in equal thirds. Two keyframe presentations left one slot stale, seen as patches flickering on a still screen.
7. **Dirty hint** — `chimera/src/scanout.rs` (`HeadScanout::plan_dirty`, `strip_hashes_within`, `strip_hash`) and `chimera/src/session.rs` (`ControlSession::present_rgb_dirty`): when the caller knows which areas changed (ScreenCaptureKit's dirty rects), only strips meeting them are hashed. Full-surface hashing of a 4K frame for a ticking menu-bar item was the largest steady CPU cost. `plan` and `present_rgb` keep upstream behaviour.
8. **Borrow cached strip bodies** — `chimera/src/scanout.rs`, `chimera/src/kvino/kernel_tree/api.rs`, and `chimera/vino/video/haar/records.rs`: frame packing accepts `AsRef<[u8]>` strip bodies and reads the cache by reference instead of cloning each body and then copying it again into a `KVec`. Existing owned-vector callers remain supported by the generic API; packing order, codec bytes, and record boundaries are unchanged. The structural reduction is two body allocations and two body copies per selected cached strip. Owned-versus-borrowed byte-equality regressions cover keyframes and damage across Ella/Ridge/Navarro, both depths and connector selectors.
9. **Pack directly into USB chunks** — `chimera/src/session.rs`: `prefix_frame` fills the final 65536-byte transfers directly rather than building a complete contiguous stream and copying it into transfers. Part order, trailer phases, and exact chunk boundaries are unchanged; a hardware-free regression compares against the former concatenation algorithm at transfer-boundary cases on all three supported dock families. Eliminates one full-stream allocation/copy by construction; no runtime/RSS measurements or dock validation performed for this patch.
10. **Retain cancelled IN transfers until completion** — `vino-driver/src/usb.rs`: teardown no longer frees transfers, their buffers, or callback state after an arbitrary 500 ms when callbacks remain outstanding. It waits until every submitted transfer is returned, matching the existing OUT cleanup rule. A hardware-free regression uses a real allocated libusb transfer and the real cancellation callback delayed beyond 500 ms. Cleanup can wait indefinitely if libusb never returns a cancelled transfer; releasing callback-owned memory instead is not safe.
11. **Bound queued device replies** — `vino-driver/src/usb.rs`: retain at most 256 EP84 replies (at most 2 MiB of payload at the existing 8192-byte transfer size). A device flooding IN while OUT pumps events could previously grow the queue without bound. Overflow clears queued data, stops rearming completed IN transfers, and makes receive fail with the existing USB overflow error rather than silently dropping a push and continuing an out-of-sync session. Added hardware-free queue-order/capacity/fail-closed coverage. The limit is a defensive ceiling, not a measured legitimate high-water mark; hardware validation remains outstanding.
12. **Present stage timings** — `chimera/src/session.rs` (`PresentTiming`, `ControlSession::last_present`) and `chimera/src/scanout.rs` (`HeadScanout::last_plan_coarse`): `present_rgb_dirty` reads the clock around plan, encode, report/transfer packing, `submit_video` and the status poll, and records whether the plan was patch 13's coarse superset, for the engine's performance counters. The timings themselves change no call order, wire bytes or return values.
13. **Coarse delta instead of keyframe fallback** — `chimera/src/scanout.rs` (`plan_dirty`, `coarse_owed_rects`): change too scattered for `MAX_RECTS` exact rectangles is planned as a delta of at most `MAX_RECTS` band rectangles covering every owing strip, presented once, instead of a keyframe presented `keyframe_presentations` (3) times back to back. This changes wire output for such frames: fewer presentations and bytes, the same record format. The retransmit debt still carries each changed strip to every dock buffer, and the settle pass is unchanged; the superset only resends strips the dock already holds. Measured on the M/Connect 2 with two HP Z27k G3 at 3840×2160@60 during App Exposé and desktop swipes (engine performance counters, busy seconds, median): head 0 went from 17 to 44 presents/s (worst second 14 → 30) and head 1 from 22 to 29 (11 → 18), with keyframe fallbacks 7/s → 0, USB time per present 20.9 → 11.2 ms and total video 66.5 → 47.6 MB/s; no dock reset or engine error was logged. Regression test: `scattered_change_is_a_coarse_delta_that_reaches_every_buffer`. `cargo test --locked -p vino-chimera` (28 tests) passes from `engine/`.

Hardware-free checks passed for patches 8–11: `cargo test --locked -p vino-chimera` (27 tests) and `cargo test --locked -p vino-driver` (8 tests), from `engine/`; the root engine dependency enables `live`. A temporary optimized-build benchmark packed the same patterned 3840×2160 Ridge frame 50 times: the former copying path took 204.1 ms, borrowed packing 119.2 ms. Each frame avoids 16,200 strip-body allocations and 41,988,360 copied body bytes by construction. This is a packing microbenchmark, not a full rendering benchmark or a process-RSS measurement; no dock was attached. The temporary benchmark was removed after measurement.

Tried and reverted (measured worse on this dock): a zero-length packet after full-packet frames (did not stop resets), presenting each delta twice (`FrameDelivery::new(2, 2, 3)`; doubled bandwidth and reset the dock without the rate limit).

To refresh, re-copy those directories from a newer upstream commit, re-apply the patches, update the commit above, and re-run `cargo test -p vino-chimera` in `engine/`. The vendored crate cannot build standalone because its optional Linux `revdi` dependency is not vendored; build it through `engine/`.
